heroHeadline: CRISPR Gene Therapy Reduces Hereditary Angioedema Attacks in Trial, Expanding Disease Indications; FDA Issues Landmark Draft Guidance to Accelerate CRISPR Gene Therapy Pipeline via Platform Data Sharing; Intellia lonvo-z Phase 3 Data Headed to EAACI Istanbul; Metagenomi MGX-001 Hemophilia A IND Q4 2026; Caribou CB-011 RMAT 92% ORR in Myeloma
heroSubtitle: June 2, 2026: FDA CBER issued the first-ever draft guidance enabling genome-editing gene therapy sponsors to leverage prior platform CMC, nonclinical, and clinical data in new regulatory submissions — covering CRISPR-Cas9, base editing, prime editing, and all gene-editing modalities. Acting Director Karim Mikhail: 'We are accelerating innovation without compromising rigorous scientific standards.' Public comment open through ~September 1, 2026. June 1, 2026: Intellia Therapeutics announced lonvoguran ziclumeran (lonvo-z) additional Phase 3 HAELO data will be presented in a late-breaking oral at the EAACI Annual Congress, Istanbul (June 13) — advancing the rolling BLA for what would be the world's first approved in vivo CRISPR gene therapy (Phase 3: 87% HAE attack reduction, 62% attack-free vs 11% placebo; U.S. launch targeted H1 2027). June 3–4, 2026: Industry pipeline showcased at Jefferies Global Healthcare Conference — CRISPR Therapeutics (CEO Samarth Kulkarni, June 3) presented Casgevy's 500+ patients and expanding cardiovascular/CAR-T pipeline; Metagenomi Therapeutics (June 4) highlighted MGX-001 hemophilia A using a compact AAV-compatible CRISPR nuclease (NHP: curative FVIII, no off-targets), IND Q4 2026; Caribou Biosciences (June 4) presented vispa-cel RMAT pivotal alignment and CB-011's 92% ORR in myeloma plus CB-010 expansion into lupus nephritis. June 3: Prime Medicine announced Goldman Sachs conference June 10 — PM577 Wilson disease IND/CTA filing imminent (H1 2026 target), potentially making prime editing the newest CRISPR technology to enter human trials.
footerNote: Data sourced from FDA, EMA, MHRA, NIH, peer-reviewed journals (Nature, Science, NEJM, Cell), ClinicalTrials.gov, and major science outlets. Clinical data reflects published peer-reviewed results only.
